AWARD/JUDGMENT FACTUAL POSITION & PLEADINGS 1.
A DAR was filed on 19/03/2021 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of all the parties of this case.
The said DAR was related to a motor vehicular accident dated 06/10/2020 in which one Sh. Chandra Shekhar S/o Sh. Ram Lotan (hereinafter referred to as "deceased") lost his life.

Subsequent to the filing of DAR, the present petition was filed on 03/08/2021 U/s 166 r/w Section 140 of M.V. Act seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 50,00,000/- under Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 in respect of the untimely death of the deceased in a motor vehicular accident which took place on 06/10/2020 at about 1.10 AM at a spot Thana Road in front of MCD Parking, Near Gali Pipal Wali, Motia Khan, Sadar Bazar, Delhi-110006 falling within the jurisdiction of PS Sadar Bazar Delhi.
As per this petition, on unfortunate day of 06.10.2020 at about 04:14 AM.

The accident was occurred at Sadar Thana Road, in front of the MCD Parking, Near Pipal Wali Gali, Motia Khan,
Sadar Bazar, Delhi when deceased was going on foot.
In the meantime offending Truck bearing registration No. HR-55U-1008 ( MACT No. 868/21 Reeta & Ors. Vs. Saddam & Ors.

It is further stated that the information was given to nearby police officials and the offending truck driver alongwith his truck was handed over to the police.

8. I have perused the record and my issue wise findings are as under:-
"Whether the deceased Sh. Chander Shekhar suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 06/10/2020 at about 04.14 A.M. involving vehicle bearing registration No. HR-55U-1008 driven by the Respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the Respondent No. 2 and insured with the Respondent No. 3?
OPP.''

9. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a MACT No. 868/21 Reeta & Ors. Vs. Saddam & Ors.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC)

15. In view of the postmortem report pertaining to the deceased placed on record by the petitioners,
no dispute is left regarding the death of the deceased on account of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.

COMPENSATION 18.

The compensation to which the petitioners are entitled shall be under the following heads:-
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY 19.
In this regard, the petitioners have examined petitioner no. 1 as PW-1 who was the wife of deceased.
PW-1 deposed that at the relevant time, the deceased was 42 years old, was self employed and was earning a sum of Rs. 20,000/- per month.
However, there is no material available on record which could corroborate the claim of PW-1 as to the monthly earnings of the deceased.

As such, it would be appropriate to assess the income of the deceased as per the minimum wages payable to a Un-Skilled Person in Delhi in terms of the judgment titled as National Insurance Company Ltd Vs Rajada & Ors passed in MAC.App 9662/2013 by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi and the petitioners have also placed on record the Praman Patr Ex.PW1/3 as per which the deceased was working in Delhi for his livelihood at the relevant time i.e. 06/10/2020, the minimum wages payable to an Un-Skilled Person in Delhi were Rs.15,492/- per month.

opennyai_summary.facts:
A DAR was filed on 19/03/2021 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of all the parties of this case.
The said DAR was related to a motor vehicular accident dated 06/10/2020 in which one Sh. Chandra Shekhar S/o Sh. Ram Lotan (hereinafter referred to as "deceased") lost his life.
Subsequent to the filing of DAR, the present petition was filed on 03/08/2021 U/s 166 r/w Section 140 of M.V. Act seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 50,00,000/- under Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 in respect of the untimely death of the deceased in a motor vehicular accident which took place on 06/10/2020 at about 1.10 AM at a spot Thana Road in front of MCD Parking, Near Gali Pipal Wali, Motia Khan, Sadar Bazar, Delhi-110006 falling within the jurisdiction of PS Sadar Bazar Delhi.
Vs. Saddam &
Ors.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Predecessor of this Tribunal :-
1.Whether the deceased Sh. Chander Shekhar suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 06/10/2020 at about 04.14 A.M. involving vehicle bearing registration No. HR-55U-1008 driven by the Respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the Respondent No. 2 and insured with the Respondent No. 3?
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
3.Relief.
8. I have perused the record and my issue wise findings are as under:-
"Whether the deceased Sh. Chander Shekhar suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 06/10/2020 at about 04.14 A.M. involving vehicle bearing registration No. HR-55U-1008 driven by the Respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the Respondent No. 2 and insured with the Respondent No. 3?
OPP.''
"Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?"
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
9. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a MACT No. 868/21 Reeta & Ors. Vs. Saddam & Ors.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC)
303.
10.
In totality, the testimony of PW-3 seems reliable and worth acting upon.
Since, PW-3 has categorically stated that the deceased Chander Shekhar died due to rash and negligent driving of R-1.
11.
Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
13.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time the deceased had died due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by R-1.
14.
Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of R-1,
if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.
In the absence of any evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased, the MACT No. 868/21 Reeta & Ors.
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
16. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the deceased lost his life on account of neglect and default of R-1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
As such, it would be appropriate to assess the income of the deceased as per the minimum wages payable to a Un-Skilled Person in Delhi in terms of the judgment titled as National Insurance Company Ltd Vs Rajada & Ors passed in MAC.App 9662/2013 by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi and the petitioners have also placed on record the Praman Patr Ex.PW1/3 as per which the deceased was working in Delhi for his livelihood at the relevant time i.e. 06/10/2020, the minimum wages payable to an Un-Skilled Person in Delhi were Rs.15,492/- per month.
20.
Going by the said documents of the MACT No. 868/21 Reeta & Ors. Vs. Saddam & Ors.
Hence, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.,
(2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, decided on 31.10.2017, the multiplier of '14' is held applicable for calculating the loss of dependency caused to the petitioners on account of death of the deceased.
21. Coming to the dependency of deceased at the time of accident, it may be observed that the deceased is survived by his wife, children and parents.
All are considered to be dependent upon the deceased.
Further, in view of subsequent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd Vs Satinder Kaur & Ors MANU/HC/0500/2020 and The New India Assurance Company Ltd & Ors Vs Somwati & Ors MANU/HC/0674/2020, the petitioners are also entitled to compensation under the head "loss of consortium": -
Spousal Consortium : Rs. 48,000/- (Rs. 48,000/- X 1)
However, since the offending vehicle was insured with R-3 at the time of accident, therefore, R-3/ Insurance Company is liable to indemnify R-2 in respect of above liability.
